- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; increase forecast to reflect mean reversion toward recent highs.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overcorrects downward; delay or reduce downward adjustment to avoid premature mean reversion.
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., +0.33 to -0.33 within 3 days), model often fails to adjust forecast mid-cycle; apply smoothing or lagged sentiment weighting to avoid abrupt shifts.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overpredict early in the horizon when sentiment is volatile; cap forecast at 1–2 standard deviations above recent 14-day moving average to avoid extreme outliers.
- When sentiment is consistently positive over 5+ days, model often fails to account for eventual pullback; add a 1–3% downward bias for the final 5–7 days of forecast.
